research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
team defensive trait stability and reliability across seasons
regression to the mean in half-level scoring differences
game-state and opponent-quality confounding of defensive effects
methodological_questions: Is a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change reliable across seasons or split halves?
How much of H2-H1 variance is defense-attributable versus noise, regression to the mean, opponent quality, or game script?
Does the team-season sample (120 units) give enough power for a reliability estimate?
Are H2-H1 differences confounded by score margin, pace, or garbage-time substitutions?

historical_evidence.finding: Trigger attribution of the H1->H2 PPP collapse. RTM (ppp_h1 alone) explained 32.9% of variance; usage, process-plus-shot-zone, lineup and context added 0.0 to 1.7 points. Unexplained variance was 65.4%, attributed to idiosyncratic noise from small per-half n. Verdict: null, classed as an adequately powered null (n=40963 cells; 12617 triggers).

Adapter PPP lift test with wrong-way, neutral, no-signal and adapter groups. Next-game PPP difference was not significant (Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842). Failure mechanism recorded as C_artifact (apparent effect produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw).

Within-game (61.0%) and cross-game (67.7%) defensive scheme changes were inferred from labels. Almost all units (99.0%) and series (52/52) showed a change, and transition matrices were near-uniform. The record notes the label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.

Post-hoc matched-pair comparison of teams that abandoned versus continued a suppressed play type. At caliper 0.10, group A excess was +0.076 (n=3421), group B excess was +0.014 with CI including 0 (n=255 pairs, 242 games, p=0.386). The group B cohort was reconstructed post hoc.

Play-type label backfill verification over 921,514 possessions. PNR share 28.7% (band 20-28%) and PULL_UP 7.9% both failed their checks; team identity failed; the final verdict was FAIL, and 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy-calibrated.

Player-level BEST versus AVOID PPP gap in 55-series initiator data: pooled gap +0.427 PPP in the same direction as the team gap, but only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. This is a different estimand from the question posed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether an adapter response produces a real PPP lift that carries over across games, including asymmetry, confidence-gradient and next-game carryover tests.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the apparent effect was produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw. Next-game carryover was not significant (p=0.842).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring defensive scheme change within and across games from inferred labels.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable. The inferred label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive behaviour, and near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Post-hoc matched-pair test of adaptation (abandoning a suppressed play type) against continued suppression.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable. The successful-adaptation group had a CI including 0 and was a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, not a validated sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using backfilled play-type labels as the measurement basis.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact with final verdict FAIL. Distribution and team-identity checks failed, so label error threatens any analysis built on them.

evidence_establishes: Half-to-half PPP change in the closest recorded study (FAM:SF-APPS-076) is dominated by regression-to-the-mean and unexplained noise. Observable process, usage, lineup and context variables added only about 1.7 points of explained variance.
Derived defensive or play-type labels in this project have failed validation or been recorded as unanswerable (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPA-005), so label quality is a live threat.
Post-hoc adaptation and carryover designs in this project did not yield a validated defensive effect (FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF-APPA-001).
The available records do not test a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change directly.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a team-level defensive H2-H1 effect exists or is stable across seasons. No retrieved record estimates a team-season defensive H2-H1 effect or its year-to-year correlation.
The reliability of any defensive effect with a split-half or season-to-season design.
Any power calculation for the 120 team-season units.
Whether opponent quality or pace explains defensive H2-H1 differences, since none of the retrieved records examines defense on this outcome.
own_inferences: The closest prior record suggests a low signal-to-noise ratio for half-level changes, which makes a high reliability estimate unlikely unless the defensive effect is large.
A reliability test across 120 team-seasons (about 90 season-to-season pairs) can detect a correlation of about 0.3 with reasonable power, but not smaller effects.

The question's wording ('reliable team trait') is an estimand about between-team variance of a shrunken effect, not a hypothesis that a single estimate is significant. This needs an explicit reliability definition before analysis.
Playoff data are partial and the 2025-26 playoffs are not complete as of the analysis date, so they should be excluded from the primary test.
uncertainties: No retrieved record directly addresses defense-side H2-H1 reliability, so the historical evidence is indirect.
The records do not state the number of possessions per team-half, so the per-team noise level is unknown.
Label provenance for defensive matchups and the defensive-matchup minutes field is not described in any retrieved record.
Rule and pace changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may create drift that is not characterised.
The status values of records outside this set were not retrieved, so the record set may be incomplete.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence moved the decision from a plain test to a proceed-with-changes plan. The records show that half-level PPP changes are noise-dominated (FAM:SF-APPS-076), that defensive labels have failed validation (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPA-005), and that post-hoc adaptation designs were not sound (FAM:SF-APPS-025, FAM:SF-APPA-001). The test therefore requires shrinkage, regression-to-the-mean control, regular-season-only data, and a validated label source before analysis.

blocking_constraints.text: Half-level PPP changes are dominated by regression to the mean. A raw correlation of H2-H1 change across seasons would be inflated or deflated; a split-half design with shrinkage is required.
With 120 team-seasons (about 90 season pairs), only moderate reliability (r about 0.3 or more) is detectable; smaller reliabilities cannot be resolved.
The defensive H2-H1 measure is built from noisy per-half PPP, and split-half reliability of the team-level metric is not established.
Score margin, garbage-time substitution, pace, and opponent quality can drive H2-H1 differences without any defensive effect.
Defensive matchup and play-type labels have failed prior validation (FAM:SF-APPA-030), so the defensive attribution could be mislabelled.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait. FAM:SF-APPS-076 (rejected, B_powered_null) finds that half-level PPP collapse is mostly unexplained noise and regression to the mean, which bears on reliability. FAM:SF-APPA-030 and FAM:SF-APPA-005 show that the label sources needed for a defensive attribution are unreliable. Prior work partly answers the question by indicating a low signal-to-noise ratio, without testing the defensive reliability estimand directly.

risks.text: Selecting teams on extreme H2-H1 values inflates apparent effects; the test must use independent split halves or pre-registered shrinkage.
120 team-seasons yield limited power for reliability estimates near 0.2 to 0.3.
Split-half reliability of the team-level H2-H1 defensive measure is unknown and may be low given the noise in FAM:SF-APPS-076.
Margin, garbage time, pace and opponent quality are unadjusted in any retrieved record and can produce spurious H2-H1 differences.
Defensive matchup and play-type labels are unvalidated (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPA-005) and can misattribute defensive responsibility.
Rules, pace and play-style changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can make seasons non-comparable and bias year-to-year reliability.
Multiple half definitions, metric variants and team subsets would inflate false positives unless one primary estimand is fixed.
Placebo or falsification results in earlier work were not always reported (FAM:SF-APPS-025 and others), so a placebo test is needed to rule out spurious patterns.

design.estimand: Between-team reliability of the defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 PPP change: the correlation between shrunken team defensive effects estimated from independent halves of the season, or from consecutive seasons, after opponent, pace and margin adjustment.
design.unit: Team-season defense (30 teams x 4 seasons) using regular-season games only; defensive possessions nested within games.
design.sample: Regular-season NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs excluded. Up to 120 team-seasons, about 90 consecutive-season pairs.
design.power: With about 90 season pairs, 80% power at alpha 0.05 detects a correlation of about 0.30; the pre-registered minimum effect of interest is r at least 0.30 with 95% CI lower bound above 0.10. Power is reported after the split-half analysis.
design.controls: Adjust for opponent offensive quality, pace, starting-lineup changes, score margin at half, garbage-time exclusion (margin above 20 in the second half), home/away and rest. Use empirical-Bayes shrinkage on team effects. Recompute with derived labels validated against an independent source.
design.falsification: Placebo H1-H1 split (first-half odd versus even possessions) must show no reliability; shuffled team labels within season must give r near 0; offensive-side H2-H1 reliability is reported as a comparison baseline.
design.multiplicity: One primary estimand (between-half shrunken reliability, regular season, adjusted). All secondary definitions (other half splits, raw versus adjusted, playoffs) are reported as exploratory with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary adjusted reliability is at least 0.30 with 95% CI lower bound above 0.10, and the placebo and shuffle checks pass. Rejected if the CI upper bound is below 0.20. Otherwise uncertain. Artifact if the effect disappears after RTM shrinkage or after the placebo check fails.
design.data_version: Frozen data as of 2026-10-06: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular-season play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and box scores. Excludes playoffs and any unvalidated derived play-type labels unless validated against the independent source.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
